page: Vultr vbm-8c-132gb-v2 is a bare metal server belonging to the Bare Metal NVMe family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 2388G processor built on the x86_64 architecture, featuring 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at a base frequency of 3.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, which translates to 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is comprised of a 3840 GB NVMe SSD, and the configuration does not include a dedicated GPU.

Performance benchmarks show strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and bzip3 single-threaded decompression scoring in the top 25%. Single-threaded gzip compression reaches top-tier status in the top 10% at 36.27 GB/sec. Multi-core performance, PassMark CPU scores, and Redis SET operations fall within the average range. However, memory bandwidth tests reveal a bottleneck, with large-block read and write operations performing in the bottom 25%, indicating potential latency under heavy, uncached memory-intensive workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this bare metal configuration offers high resource density, combining a large 3.8 TB NVMe storage capacity with dedicated physical cores. This makes it a viable option for workloads requiring direct hardware access without virtualization overhead. It is well-suited for relational databases, local caching layers, static web serving, and lightweight text-generation tasks, though applications requiring massive, continuous memory bandwidth may experience performance trade-offs.
